title: Local Law - San Francisco
description: SF Rent Ordinance, Rent Board rules, licensing, banking and petitions.

rows.label: Coverage cutoff
rows.value: Many units built on/before June 13, 1979 have rent control and eviction protection
rows.notes: Verify exact address in PIM; partial exemptions exist.

rows.label: Annual increase
rows.value: 1.6% once every 12 months on anniversary date
rows.notes: Current rate.

rows.label: Ordinance cap
rows.value: 60% CPI, max 7%
rows.notes: SF Admin Code 37.3.

rows.label: Initial rent
rows.value: No limit on first rent for vacant covered unit
rows.notes: Not a reset for an existing tenancy.

rows.label: License
rows.value: Current Rent Increase License required when an annual/banked increase takes effect
rows.notes: Rule 13.14 tests the effective date, not the service date.

rows.label: Housing Inventory
rows.value: Annual report by March 1; license auto-generated for non-owner-occupied units
rows.notes: No monetary penalty, but notice unenforceable without license.

rows.label: Banking
rows.value: SF guidance distinguishes skipped increases (24 full months without an increase) from unused portions of partial increases (at least 12 months later or a future anniversary). Add eligible percentages; do not compound or prorate.
rows.notes: Notice must identify the banked portion; see the pending proposal.

rows.label: Additional occupants
rows.value: No extra rent merely because new/additional roommate moved in
rows.notes: Even if lease says otherwise.

rows.label: Pending legislation (proposed, not law)
rows.value: File 261020 would cap combined banked plus capital improvement increases at 10% per year; version 1, 'Pending Committee Action' on 2026-11-10
rows.notes: Proposed only - creates no current limit. See Rates page RATE-12 to RATE-18 and flags F46/F47.

rows.label: Petition grounds
rows.value: Capital improvement, O&M, comparable rents, Proposition I, utility, 1.21, bond/water passthroughs
rows.notes: Petition/worksheet before notice.

rows.label: Section 6.14 and Costa-Hawkins
rows.value: Section 6.14 and Costa-Hawkins have distinct requirements when the last original occupant leaves. Section 6.14 requires timely written notice to remaining occupants; Costa-Hawkins addresses qualifying subtenants or assignees, not co-tenants.
rows.notes: Whether either path applies is fact-specific and unverified; SF.gov urges legal advice.

rows.label: Costa-Hawkins local view
rows.value: Co-tenants not subject; qualifying post-1995 subtenant/assignee only
rows.notes: Legal advice strongly encouraged.

rows.label: Tenant harassment
rows.value: Bad-faith coercion/discrimination/privacy interference prohibited
rows.notes: Larson footnote conflict flagged.

rows.label: Tenant petition
rows.value: No charge, no time limit, ALJ hearing
rows.notes: 516C and 518 forms.

rows.label: Ordinance text 37.15
rows.value: Owners report under penalty of perjury; condominiums and units in buildings under 10 units report from March 1, 2023 and annually by March 1; compliant owners receive a license to impose rent increases; otherwise the license is suspended and the tenant is not obligated to pay the increased rent for months during the suspension
rows.notes: Added by Ord. 265-20; not a rental registry under Civil Code 1947.7-1947.8.

rows.label: Rent Board Fee is separate from the license
rows.value: Every residential dwelling unit owner pays a per-unit fee unless exempt: 2026-2027 is $59.00 per dwelling unit, due March 1, 5% late penalty per month to a 15% maximum; a fee exemption does not satisfy Housing Inventory reporting
rows.notes: Two separate obligations; see flag F33.

rows.label: Recovering half the fee
rows.value: If the fee is paid in full, 50% ($29.50 per dwelling unit for 2026-2027) may be recovered from tenants in occupancy as of November 1 of the tax year; penalties may not be recovered
rows.notes: Not a rent increase; identify it separately on any statement.

rows.label: Units built after June 13, 1979
rows.value: Exempt from the rent increase limitations only, if the first Certificate of Occupancy issued after June 13, 1979 and there was no prior residential use; just-cause eviction protection and the Rent Board fee still apply
rows.notes: The owner-supplied 1940 year would fall before the cutoff if confirmed.

rows.label: In-law unit or second structure on the lot
rows.value: A single-family dwelling with a LEGAL in-law unit is a two-unit building and is not exempt. With an ILLEGAL in-law unit it is also a two-unit building and is not exempt UNLESS both units are rented together as a single tenancy. A single-family dwelling is not exempt if another residential structure is on the same lot
rows.notes: Wording corrected 2026-11-08 against the page; two rented units is consistent with coverage (flags F35, F36).

rows.label: 30-day update duty
rows.value: A change in the owner or designated manager name or business contact information must be reported within 30 days
rows.notes: Separate from the annual March 1 update.

rows.label: License scope
rows.value: License rules apply only to rent-controlled units; SF.gov says the license is not required for 6.14/Costa-Hawkins increases or petition-based passthroughs
rows.notes: Those increases have separate rules and remedies.

rows.label: Housing Inventory data is public
rows.value: Submission information is public, including name and business contact details
rows.notes: Privacy consideration before filing.

rows.label: Multiple-year increases
rows.value: Landlords are not required to file a petition to impose multi-year banked increases; add the allowable percentages; no compounding; no rounding up
rows.notes: 30-day notice (35 if mailed).

rows.label: Where to file and check
rows.value: Rent Board Portal account; report inventory; look up license status by address or APN; paper filings by email or office drop-off
rows.notes: Office open 9-4 weekdays; counseling 415-252-4600.
